identification: PostgreSQL pg_cron, SECURITY DEFINER and WAL-archiver exploit reconstructions
basis: The contents attempt scheduler impersonation as postgres, caller-controlled owner-privileged SQL, elevated role membership, account-file reading, and replacing server auto-configuration with an identity-probe shell command. No ordinary database maintenance result explains that combination. These are explicit exploit attempts, with important defects; successful compromise or a deployed malware family is not established.
context_missing: Registry package coordinates and original distribution context
Target PostgreSQL version, role grants, pg_cron installation/preload and job state
Whether statements were executed manually in stages
obfuscation: None. Python raw triple-quoted SQL and PowerShell single-quoted here-string preserve the payload. Nested PostgreSQL dollar quotes delimit SQL bodies and configuration data; they are not encryption. cleave facts exposed the SQL and no additional encoded payload.

execution_paths.driver-variant.py: At module load reads DATABASE_URL, calls psycopg.connect(autocommit=True), then passes all SQL to one conn.execute call. There is no wait, retry, result handling, or staged second connection. psycopg sends this parameter-free batch as one transaction: newly registered cron work is not visible to another worker before commit. An undefined definer-function call can abort and roll back the preceding database changes.
execution_paths.powershell-client.ps1: Assigns a literal here-string to $sql, pipes it to the psql executable using the call operator, and sets ON_ERROR_STOP=1. psql sends complete statements separately; early commits are possible, but a fresh run normally reaches the definer call before the next cron tick and stops on error. Connection selection comes from psql defaults/environment, not a hardcoded attacker endpoint.
execution_paths.reconstructed-chain.sql: The same staged chain as raw SQL, with different function/role names and OID. It requires a SQL client. Whether execution continues after an error depends on that client; the comment instructs waiting but provides no synchronization.

shared_chain: GRANT pg_read_all_data and pg_write_all_data requires existing grant authority; it does not itself bypass permissions.
CREATE EXTENSION pg_cron and cron.schedule require installation/configuration/privileges. The fixed WHERE jobid=1 does not use the newly returned job ID and may select no job or another job.

UPDATE cron.job sets username=postgres and stores a DO block that creates a SECURITY DEFINER function, then grants its use to an application role. The function returns dynamic SQL results as its owner if the scheduled creation succeeds.

The subsequent SELECT requests a superuser-named role GRANT through RETURN QUERY EXECUTE. Such GRANT does not return tuples and fails on tested PostgreSQL; the role names also require target-specific existence and authority.

The pg_read_file and lo_export LANGUAGE internal declarations express attempted server-file access. Both supplied internal names are invalid on tested stock PostgreSQL 18.6; actual symbols are pg_read_file_off_len and be_lo_export. Creating internal-language functions also requires elevated authority. Rebinding a read symbol does not remove its runtime path/role checks.

The final intended path stages archive_command data in a large object, invokes an export alias targeting the mandated postgresql.auto.conf name, reloads configuration, and switches WAL. A working export could overwrite the file rather than append to it. Archiver shell execution requires appropriate preexisting archive settings; the scripts do not enable archive_mode. id redirects a probe to /tmp, not an exfiltration endpoint.

isolated_verification.method: Fresh scratch cluster with TCP disabled and a private Unix socket. Only isolated function/transaction fragments and dummy roles were evaluated; no sample was run against a real deployment, no pg_cron job was installed, no account file was read, and no archiver payload was installed. Server was stopped afterward.
results: Exact maintenance_query function body with SELECT current_user::text returned owner reviewer.
The same body with GRANT higher_role TO lower_role raised GRANT ROLE query does not return tuples; pg_has_role remained false.
A single multi-statement command containing CREATE TABLE then an undefined function left no table, confirming batch rollback.
AS pg_read_file and AS lo_export internal declarations both failed even as cluster superuser: no built-in function of that name.
A schema-authorized ordinary role attempting a correct be_lo_export internal binding was denied permission for language internal.

trait_changes: Moved 15 observations from the database-engine directory to their supported operation/subject homes, including SQL row updates, stored-code declarations, security grants, query calls, database configuration/archiving, and source assignment syntax.
Moved the targeted cron username rewrite from query to write/row. Renamed the generic postgres username assignment to avoid claiming it belongs to a job.
Consolidated the duplicate definer matcher into the canonical statement-bounded matcher; separate restricted-definer and dynamic invoker functions no longer establish definer-dynamic SQL.
Consolidated overlapping auto-config argument observations into a SELECT-call matcher, avoiding a bare parenthesized pair being named an output operation.

Cron hostile evidence now also requires a dollar-quoted DO command assignment; archiver hostile evidence requires a same-call large-object/convert_to/archive_command staging shape, same-declaration internal export, a config reload and a WAL switch, plus exploit context.
File binding descriptions explicitly describe declarations, not successful native-symbol resolution. Matchers also recognize correct be_lo_export and pg_read_file_off_len/all variants.
Corrected /etc/passwd read matcher description to its read-prefixed call evidence and removed unsupported current-user ATT&CK mapping.

Intentional suppression correction: existing PostgreSQL-directory exclusions remain limited to retained database-runtime/client facts. Moved SQL-operation observations are not copied into unrelated loader, syscall, PATH or ransomware suppressors: SQL syntax does not identify a benign database runtime. This is a dependency-population change, not a placement-only preservation claim.

checks.focused_cases: 12 passed, including 4 exploit carriers/variants and 8 controls/near misses.
checks.final_atomscan: All 3 full sample paths rescanned using local traits; exactly 2 hostile findings each. Exit status 1 represents the detection result; JSON reports were checked.
